history.text: what does set -euo pipefail actually do
`-e` exits on the first command that fails, `-u` makes unset variables an error, and `-o pipefail` makes a pipeline fail when any command in it fails, not just the last one.
diff between "$@" and "$*"
Quoted, `"$@"` expands to each argument as its own word, so arguments with spaces survive. `"$*"` joins all arguments into one string separated by the first character of IFS.
why does everyone use [[ ]] over [ ]

`[[ ]]` is a bash keyword: no word splitting or globbing inside it, and it supports `&&`, `||` and regex matching with `=~`. `[ ]` is the POSIX test command, so it is more portable but easier to trip over.
